transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening after my cataract surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's great that you're eager to get back to gardening! However, it's typically advised to wait at least a week or two before engaging in any activities that involve bending over or lifting heavy items. It's best to consult with your surgeon to get personalized advice depending on your recovery. Do you have another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can continue using any eye drops you were using before your operation, such as for dry eyes, unless you were told otherwise. If you’re running low, your GP should be able to provide more. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's reassuring to hear. Another thing I noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Some sensitivity to light can be normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens. If it’s just mild and things seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses outside is recommended. But significant pain in bright light, or severe light sensitivity, is not normal, especially if your eye is red and painful, and we may need to assess this further. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the clarification. One last thing — should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after your operation. It should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all I had. Thank you so much for your help and the information.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass
